Devon's Lea County Avalon permit is a step-out well where the formation's clay-reactive intervals often require a customized inhibitive water-based or synthetic mud system that Newpark has proposed but not yet contracted; reaching Devon's Delaware Basin team by mid-September provides a realistic window to offer a technical comparison before rig arrival in late September.

Marathon Oil's Dunn County pad program has historically defaulted to Baroid under a basin-wide MSA, but internal procurement data suggests Marathon issued an open RFQ for fluid services on Q4 2026 wells to pressure Baroid on day-rate pricing — this well falls squarely in that review cycle. A proposal submitted before September 5th positions a challenger vendor ahead of Marathon's internal scoring deadline and before Baroid's contract renewal clause auto-activates.

Devon's newly permitted Frio County location is part of a 6-well development program where fluids contracts are typically bundled and awarded 4-5 weeks before first spud, putting the decision around late August to early September. Halliburton Baroid is the probable awardee based on Devon's Eagle Ford MSA history, but a competitive technical proposal on HPWBM could displace them on this higher-temperature well.

Following Marathon's CrownRock integration, the Anadarko subsidiary is rationalizing its vendor list and the Hunton Lime program in Canadian County is the first well drilled under the new procurement policy, meaning the incumbent Baker Hughes relationship is not automatically guaranteed for 2026 forward. Submitting a formal mud program proposal through Marathon's OKC procurement portal before Sept 15 positions you ahead of the final contractor review meeting expected in mid-September.

Bison is an independent without a long-term fluid MSA and typically awards contracts on a well-by-well basis 3-4 weeks pre-spud, meaning the decision point lands around early-to-mid September; Newpark has been the recent incumbent, but at 14,500 ft and 218°F this is an ideal case for a high-performance HPHT water-based system pitch from Baroid or Flotek.

Vaalco is a newer entrant in the Green River Basin and has not yet established a preferred mud vendor relationship for their Wyoming assets, making this an ideal greenfield opportunity; submit a programmatic proposal covering all three permitted Mowry locations before September 15 to influence the master service agreement before Baroid's regional rep closes the deal.

SM Energy's deep Cline target is one of the most thermally demanding wells in the basin this cycle at 235°F, and Newpark's EVOLUTION high-performance WBM is their expected offering—however SM issued an RFQ for deep Wolfcamp/Cline fluids in late July suggesting no locked-in vendor. Contacting SM Energy's Midland drilling supervisor by mid-September with a high-density, high-temperature SBM or advanced inhibitive WBM technical sheet positions you ahead of the likely September 25 award decision.
